translations.text: He had very many servants, and his work on the earth was great. He was a good man in the land of the dawn, where the sun rises.
The house fell on your sons and daughters, and they died. I alone escaped and came to tell you.

But stretch out your hand and strike his bones and his flesh, and see whether he will not curse you to your face. 6. The Lord said to Satan, “Look, I have given his flesh and his bones into your hand, but spare his life.” 7. Satan went out from the Lord’s presence rejoicing, and afflicted Job with terrible sores from his feet to his head.
Because they did not close the door of my mother’s womb, and did not see [?] as it rose, and did not remove suffering from my eyes.
I had no quiet, no rest, and no safety, and scourging and suffering came upon me.
He said, “Do not speak at length while you are suffering. What good will multiplying words do you?”
The lion’s roar, the lioness’s cry, and the young lions’ majesty have perished.

The old lion too perished for lack of food, and the lion cubs perished among themselves. 12. But if you had done even one righteous deed, all this would not have surrounded you. A word arose near me, and my ear heard a sound from it. At first I did not believe the one who told me.
Fear covered me; terror and trembling seized me, and [?] my bones.
He does not trust his servants at all, and he finds fault even with his angels.
They do not survive from morning until evening. Because they cannot save or help themselves, they are destroyed.
He overturns the plans of those who act cunningly, and their hands accomplish nothing right.
Darkness meets them in the daytime. At noon they grope like a blind person, as though it were night, and they are destroyed in slaughter.
He rescues the weak from the hand of [?] the strong, giving hope to [?], and the oppressor’s mouth is shut.
He will rescue you from six troubles, and in the seventh no evil will touch you.
You will laugh at sinners and violent people. You will not fear the beasts of the field, and the beasts of the wilderness will be at peace with you.
You will know that your offspring are numerous, and your children are like the flourishing grass of the ground.
God took hold of me, finished me off, and killed me forever.
Is my flesh bronze? Or is my strength the strength of stone?
Truly, those who trust in their possessions and in their houses will be put to shame.
When I sleep, I say, “When will morning come for me?” And when I wake, I say again, “When will evening come?”
Like a cloud cleared away from the sky, a person who has gone down into the grave will not come up again.
He gained power over my soul and my spirit, and [?] my eyes. Will I live forever, so that I should endure? Go far away from me, for my life is empty.

Even if I have sinned, what then can I do to you, you who know the human heart? Why have you appointed me to receive your scourging, and why did you create me in your likeness? Yet I have become a burden to you.
If your children sinned before him, he sent them away because of their sin.
Can grass sprout without water, or can greenery grow without being watered? 12. All grass that does not drink water dries up before it is cut.
Truly, I know that this is so. But how can a righteous person be pure before God?
Even if he wished to dispute with him, he could not answer him one word out of a thousand.
If he passes by me, I do not see him; if he goes past, I do not recognize him.
I am innocent, yet I do not know myself; nevertheless, my life has perished.
And even if there is a ship, the trace of its path cannot be recognized, or an eagle flying and searching for something to eat.
If his terror did not assail me, I would speak to him, though I do not see him.
You know that I have not sinned against you, yet who can rescue me from your hand?

If only God would speak to you and open his lips to you! He would tell you the power of wisdom, for what confronts you is astonishing. 7. Then you would know that what you have received from God is what you deserved for your sins. Can you find God's tracks? Were you there before him, at the beginning, when he created the whole world and the high heavens?
What can you do, and what do you know of the depth of the abyss?
I too have understanding like you, for there is no one like God. He becomes a laughingstock to his neighbor, and the righteous, innocent man is a laughingstock.
Ask the animals whether they will tell you, and the birds of the sky whether they will teach you.
I know what you know, and I am no more foolish than you.
Will his power not frighten you in his presence, and will terror not come upon you from him?
I have gathered my flesh between my teeth and placed my life in my hands.
Listen to my words, and I will tell you while you listen to me.
Look, I have come to present my case, and I know that my innocence will be revealed.
When a man dies, he passes away; when a mortal dies, he no longer exists. 10. Even the sea has hope when it receives water, but a river dwindles and dries up.
He is given as food to vultures, and he himself does not know that a sudden blow and darkness await him.

Suffering and poverty drive him from his house, like a messenger appointed to go ahead, and he is put to shame, because he raised his hand against God and stiffened his neck before God, who rules everything. 21. His disgrace terrifies him, and in his prosperous days his strength [?].
Even now, look: my witness is in heaven, and the one who knows me is on high.
Bildad spoke again and answered. 2. He said, "How long will you refuse to be silent? Restrain yourself now, so that we too may speak to you."
Sores break out from his flesh, his misery grows, and God takes vengeance on him.
His roots dry up beneath him, and his fruit falls from above him.
Who will write down my words and inscribe them in a book forever?
And when he says, “I have finished; I am secure,” then he will perish forever, and those who know him will say, “Where is he?”
Death will drag his house away forever, and the day of youth will come upon him.
They complete their days in prosperity and sleep in the bed of Sheol. 13 And they say to God, “Stay away from us! We do not want to see your ways.”
You did not even give water to the thirsty, and you withheld bread from the hungry. The man who sows possesses the land, and the favored person lives in it.
There are also some whose faces you admired, while you hated the poor and treated them unjustly on the earth.
You sent widows away naked and afflicted orphans.
The righteous saw them and laughed, and the innocent mocked them.
But if you repent and humble yourself before God, remove injustice from your heart.
For he humbled you; you will say, “He exalted the one who humbles himself.”
What is it that [?] does not know, so that I may find and reach [?] forever?
Who will dispute with him about judgment? For he does whatever he wishes.
He weakened the mighty in his anger, and when one rises, he has no confidence in his life.
He made many mourn through his appointment, and he withers like a mallow in the heat, like an ear of grain that falls by itself from its stalk.
Those who increase [?] oppressed me; the water beneath him and what is within it are not God.
What is spread out for him [?] flies above his throne, and he places a cloud over it at all times.
He made the pillars of heaven firm, and they did not depart from his command; they tremble at his rebuke.
As long as my life remains, and the spirit of God still enables me to speak, my mouth will not speak injustice, and my soul will not learn sin.
He raised his hand against the flint and destroyed the mountains from their foundations and their roots.
Where was wisdom found, and where is the dwelling place of wisdom?
Where was wisdom found, and where is the dwelling place of understanding?
When oil flowed along my paths, and when milk poured through my mountains.
Like thirsty land that waits for rain, so they waited for my words.
I sought out their way and sat judging them. I sat alone like a king, and when they mourned, they took comfort in me.
They feed [?] because of hunger, licking [?], those who flee from the hand of the wilderness, yesterday in toil and misery.
Robbers rose against me, whose houses are in the hollows of rocks.
And now my soul is poured out within me, and anguish has overwhelmed me.
All night my bones burn, and my sinews waste away.
If I wanted to eat alone and did not let another share, let another do the same to me.
And if I saw someone naked and did not clothe him while he was dying from the cold.
Those living with me said, “Who would give us his flesh to eat?” though I was very merciful to them.
No traveler spent the night outside, and my house was open to everyone passing through. If I sinned and concealed it, let my guilt be great.
Elihu waited for them to answer Job, because they were older than he was.
They allowed the man to speak words like these.
I waited for you, but you did not speak, because you remained silent and did not answer.
I gave him something to say, and he treated me as an enemy.
For God speaks once through the prophets, and a second time in a dream, or else in a message at night.
Then he opens a person's heart so that the person sees terror and is afraid.
But he saved my soul from death, so that my life might be praised in the light.
But if not, listen to me and be silent; I will teach you wisdom.
He does not listen to those who do wrong. Present your case before him, then, if you can praise him as he is.
And now, because no one knows the time of his anger, and he does not take account of his great sin. 15 But Job speaks in vain and opens his mouth; without knowledge he multiplies his words.
I will bring back my words from afar, and I will declare my deeds righteous.
And for the little one he covers the light, and he commands it [?].
He commands snow to fall upon the earth, and the winter rain falls by his power.
He restrains everyone's hands so that every human being may know his labor.

He hides the chosen ones in a cloud and scatters the cloud with his light. He turns it in its circuit; his purpose is one in his work, in everything he has commanded them, according to the order that comes from him upon the earth.
Listen to this, Job; accept correction and stand in the power of God.
Can you strengthen your struggle with him from the south? His appearance is awesome to many.
Does he have a book and a scribe, so that I should remain silent when a man stands before me?
On what are its rings suspended, and who established its corners?
And where is the dwelling of light, and where is the place of darkness?
Do you know the course of heaven, or what happens together beneath heaven?
And again God answered Job from the cloud and said to him:
And I too will acknowledge that your right hand is able to save.
And look, his power is in his loins, and his strength is in the navel of his belly.
And who can open the doors before his face? Terror surrounds his teeth.
Hear me, and I will speak to you, my Lord. I will ask you, and you teach me.
And no women as beautiful as Job’s daughters were found beneath heaven, and their father gave them their inheritance along with their brothers.
And this is its translation from the Syriac book: the land where he lived was Uz, on the border of Edom in Arabia.
